# Platform differences

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_shared_contracts.py --write-report from
     scripts/ci/platform-differences.toml and scripts/ci/clone-baseline.toml. Do not edit by
     hand; the default check fails when this file is stale. -->

Every difference between products (Piers, Decks) must be **earned**: an
operating-system API or behaviour forces it. Anything else is a gap to
close or logic to move to `shared/`. This page is the ledger of both.

- **Earned differences** name the OS API or behaviour and cite the code.
- **Open gaps** are differences nobody has earned. Each has an owner; it
  closes when parity lands or when it is earned with evidence. "Not
  implemented yet" and "not possible" are different statements.
- `python3 scripts/check_shared_contracts.py` fails when an OS-conditional
  `cfg` in `shared/` has no row, a citation no longer holds, the
  capability matrix disagrees with the code, a new local copy of shared
  logic appears, a `platform` config key has no row, or cross-product
  clones grow past the baseline.

To add a difference, edit the ledger and run
`python3 scripts/check_shared_contracts.py --write-report`.

One shared issuer needs to renew over the SEC1 keys deployed Linux Piers hold, which rcgen with ring cannot read; a SEC1-to-PKCS #8 wrap (tested in host_material) is the route. | Shared/Architecture | `hosts/linux/src/host_cert.rs` (`ecparam`)<br>`hosts/macos/src/host_cert.rs` (`self_signed`)<br>`packaging/windows/installer/src/main.rs` (`certificate_params`)<br>`packaging/linux/installer/src/main.rs` (`recover_interrupted`) |
| GAP-039 | TLS material | macOS Pier | The macOS Pier reads its TLS material once at start: no reload and no certificate lifecycle events (active, expiring, expired, reloaded); Linux reloads on SIGHUP and Windows on its reload request, both emitting the shared events. | Not implemented yet; HostTlsMaterial::reload and startup_event/status_events are shared and need only a trigger and an emitter. | macOS Host | `hosts/macos/src/tls_material.rs` (`HostTlsMaterial::load`)<br>`shared/transport/src/host_material.rs` (`fn reload`) |
| GAP-040 | support bundle | Linux Pier, Windows Pier, macOS Pier | A Deck's support bundle can include its crash reports when asked (Settings checkbox, `--include-crash-dumps`); a Pier records the request as `crash_reports_not_collected` and includes none. | Each OS keeps a Pier's crash reports where the Pier can read them (systemd-coredump, WER LocalDumps, DiagnosticReports); only that source adapter is OS-specific. The opt-in, the manifest record and the scrubbing are shared. | Shared/Architecture | `shared/observability/src/support_bundle.rs` (`CrashReportsNotCollected`) |
| GAP-041 | session lifetime | Windows Pier, macOS Pier | Only the Linux Pier locks the session when a Deck leaves and hands the console back in the shared order (`console_session::DETACH_STEPS`); the Windows and macOS Piers never end the session but leave it unlocked (ADR 0025 audit). | Not implemented yet: the Windows agent needs LockWorkStation in the user's session at detach, the macOS agent the equivalent screen lock, each followed by the shared hand-back order. | Shared/Architecture | `shared/session/src/console_session/mod.rs` (`DETACH_STEPS`) |
| GAP-042 | session model | Linux Pier | The Linux Pier joins X11 console sessions only; a GNOME Wayland console session or login screen is refused `console_wayland_session` (ADR 0025 section 9). | Not implemented yet. Upstream has the route (Mutter ScreenCast and RemoteDesktop on the user's session bus, as GNOME Remote Desktop's desktop sharing uses; the greeter hook exists in GNOME Shell 40 and 49); Arcen's side (session-bus discovery, RecordMonitor capture of physical monitors, input through the session's RemoteDesktop session, the lock screen) is work package console-wayland. | Linux Host | `shared/session/src/console_session/mod.rs` (`WaylandSession`) |
| GAP-043 | session model | Windows Pier, macOS Pier | Only the Linux Pier names, in the refusal a Deck shows, the other remote-desktop service that holds the workstation, as the host reports it at run time (`console_session::ForeignService`, `ConsoleNotice`); the Windows Pier refuses another account at the console without naming what drives it, the macOS Pier names the console owner only. | Not implemented yet. Windows can read the console or remote session's WinStation name and protocol (`WTSQuerySessionInformationW`, already called in windows_session.rs) and the service owning the session's processes; macOS has no other-product console session model yet. Both would build the same shared ConsoleNotice. | Shared/Architecture | `shared/session/src/console_session/foreign_service.rs` (`ConsoleNotice`) |

punctuation removed), on the larger side of each pair. A pair may
shrink, never grow.
